data.exact_reserve_text: The result is driven by reserve increases in the closed years, where the 2013 and 2016 years have required reserve strengthening beyond their respective pure year close position. In contrast the 2014 and 2015 years are performing better than expected when those years were closed. Unfavourable development for 2016 is particularly disappointing and is driven by catastrophe losses, strengthening of liability reserves and a deterioration in Specialty loss ratios. This development further supports the remediation actions taken in subsequent years. The loss for the year has been impacted by movements in the 2017 and prior year accounts, coupled with the effect of tornado losses attaching to the 2018 year of account. The result for the account has been impacted by the movement in large claim reserves for the 2013 and 2014 years, and late development of certain claims from the 2015 year, as well as an adjustment to reserves on certain more specialised business. For the 2016 year, catastrophe losses, liability reserve increases and Specialty class loss ratio deterioration have specifically contributed to the loss.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross strengthening of GBP 58.418m in prior year reserves. This was primarily driven by reserve increases and unfavourable development in closed years, specifically for the 2013, 2014, 2015, and 2016 years of account. Causes included movements in large claim reserves for 2013 and 2014, late development of claims for 2015, and for 2016, catastrophe losses, strengthening of liability reserves, and deterioration in Specialty loss ratios. While some years (2014 and 2015) performed better than expected, the overall impact was a strengthening.
